title: Completion of coherent modules on a proper scheme over a complete Noetherian ring is fully faithful
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete with respect to an ideal $I$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$ the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] (the ideal sheaf generated by the images of the elements of $I$). Then the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], is fully faithful: for coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ the map $u\mapsto u^\wedge$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)$, is bijective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful); its proof uses Lemma 0882 (lemma-completion-internal-hom) and the theorem on formal functions in the form of Lemma 087U (lemma-spell-out-theorem-formal-functions; Theorem 02OC theorem-formal-functions, Section 02O7 section-theorem-formal-functions)

proof.text: (Setting.) $X$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, so that $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ and the completion functor of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] are defined. Indeed $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a Noetherian scheme (affine, hence quasi-compact, and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] since $A$ is Noetherian), $f$ is of finite type as it is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The ideal $\widetilde I\subseteq\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], so $f^*\widetilde I$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], and $\mathcal I$, the image of the map $f^*\widetilde I\to\mathcal O_X$ of quasi-coherent modules [def-nagata-extended-ideal], is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful, line 6760) (the hypotheses of Section 0EHN, section-coherent-formal, used tacitly)

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ the sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then $\mathcal H$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent], and $\Gamma(X,\mathcal H)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ by the definition of the sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful, line 6760), first sentence (Modules, Lemma 01CQ)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-internal-hom], applied to the Noetherian scheme $X$ and the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ (step 1), the map $\Phi:\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)$, $(s_n)_n\mapsto(\varepsilon_n(s_n))_n$, is bijective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful, line 6760), second sentence (Lemma 0882, lemma-completion-internal-hom)

proof.text: By the theorem on formal functions over the complete Noetherian ring $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-functions-complete-base], in degree $p=0$ and for the coherent module $\mathcal H$ (step 2), the map $\Psi:\Gamma(X,\mathcal H)\to\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)$, $u\mapsto(u\bmod\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)_n$, is bijective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful, line 6760), last sentence (Lemma 087U, lemma-spell-out-theorem-formal-functions, i.e. Theorem 02OC)

proof.text: The composite $\Phi\circ\Psi:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal H)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)$ is $u\mapsto u^\wedge$: by the definition of $\varepsilon_n$ in [lem-weil-pbc-completion-internal-hom], $\varepsilon_n(u\bmod\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)$ is the map $\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ induced by $\pi_n\circ u$, which is $u\bmod\mathcal I^n$, the $n$-th component of $u^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2). As $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are bijective (steps 3, 4), $u\mapsto u^\wedge$ is bijective for all coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, i.e. the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is fully faithful.
